C005.name: Emerging jets and dark showers (GeV dark pions, Higgs portal, triggers)
frameworks: Dark QCD (hidden valley), bifundamental mediators, Higgs-portal dark showers
Dark QCD / semi-visible jets
QCD-like dark sector / scalar portal
confining dark sector with vector-like dark quarks charged under SU(2)L (Drell-Yan production)
ideas: Snowmass dark-shower report states parameter space is largely unconstrained for dark pion masses above a few GeV in both prompt and long-lived regimes. Existing CMS searches target low-mass (dimuon) or emerging jets; intermediate masses with hadronic displaced decays and soft multiplicity are less covered.

EW pair production of heavy dark quarks Q_u Q_d (W exchange) yields dark showers plus leptons/MET with cross section not suppressed by QCD colour; HL-LHC may reach ~1 TeV mediators. Existing emerging-jet search assumes QCD-coloured mediators.

Emerging-jet taggers have been developed for QCD-produced t-channel mediators; Higgs-portal production (ggF, VBF, VH) offers cleaner triggers and is not a target of the CMS EJ analysis per the HL-LHC-oriented study.
Current triggers define which parts of dark-QCD parameter space are visible; Phase-2 L1 tracking, L1 scouting and timing may open regions. Study of trigger choices indicates blind spots.
signature_hypotheses: Displaced multi-track vertices / jets with high track multiplicity from boosted dark showers; trackless displaced jets; ML anomaly tagging of dark-shower jets
Displaced/emerging-jet-like activity plus isolated lepton or MET in EW-like production; track-multiplicity vertex tagging with Drell-Yan topologies
VBF/VH-tagged Higgs with displaced multi-vertex jets; two displaced-vertex jets with m_jj ~ 125 GeV; HL-LHC with MTD timing

ideas: Quirks lose energy and annihilate out-of-time; existing out-of-time R-hadron search recast; regime with long strings left for future work.

Quirks with EW charge and masses of a few hundred GeV are unconstrained; signals include non-helical tracks, soft unclustered energy patterns and trigger-dependent muon signals. First collider-experiment quirk search came from FASER (2026).

Electroweakly charged quirks with long strings give non-standard tracks/deposits (soft unclustered energy, displaced/curved tracks); Run-2 style searches did not cover regions even after HL-LHC according to authors.

Heavy quarks charged under both SM and a confining hidden gauge group stay connected by a macroscopic string; pairs oscillate, lose energy in matter and annihilate late, giving non-standard tracks (bending, ionisation, out-of-time decays). Theory papers 2008-2018 proposed several strategies; the 2026 FASER result is the only LHC-experiment quirk search I found, none from ATLAS/CMS in my INSPIRE query.
signature_hypotheses: out-of-time energy deposits, anomalous ionisation, bent tracks
Non-helical/ anomalous tracks with ionisation, SUEP-like soft energy from quirk annihilation, large-radius muon-trigger events

C051.name: High-mass DY angular coefficients (Lam-Tung, T-odd A5-A7) and A_FB/sin2theta running
frameworks: SMEFT dim-6 (dipole, scalar/tensor four-fermion) and dim-8
SMEFT dim-8 CP-odd semileptonic four-fermion + gluon field strength; dim-6 EW x chromomagnetic dipole interference
SMEFT four-fermion operators, SM EW running, off-peak A_FB
ideas: Chirality-breaking operators (dipoles, scalar/tensor four-fermion) do not interfere with the SM in unpolarised rates but break the Lam-Tung relation A0=A2 in the Collins-Soper angular decomposition. Existing angular-coefficient measurements are at the Z peak; the energy-growing region (high m_ll, high pT_ll) has not been unfolded.

A5-A7 vanish at tree level in the SM and are loop-suppressed; dim-8 CP-odd operators with a gluon field strength, and O(1/Lambda^4) EW-dipole x chromomagnetic-dipole interference, populate them in the high mass / high pT region.
Off-peak A_FB(m_ll) provides both SMEFT four-fermion sensitivity (growth with m_ll^2/Lambda^2) and a test of the time-like running of the weak mixing angle above m_Z, which has not been probed.
signature_hypotheses: Unfolded A0-A7 (esp. A0-A2) double-differential in m_ll (>200 GeV) and pT_ll, e and mu channels, at 13/13.6 TeV and HL-LHC
A6 and A7 (and A5) vs m_ll and pT_ll above Z peak; sign-sensitive asymmetries in cos(theta)sin(phi)
